concepts.title: Adding & Subtracting Fractions (Unlike Denominators)
know: To add or subtract fractions with different denominators, first rewrite them as equivalent fractions with a common denominator.
Multiply the top and bottom of a fraction by the same number to make an equivalent fraction — the value does not change.
Never add or subtract the denominators. The denominator just tells the size of the pieces.
For mixed numbers, add or subtract the whole numbers and fractions separately, or rewrite everything as improper fractions.
Use benchmark fractions like 0, {{1/2}}, and 1 to estimate answers and catch mistakes.
Always give your final answer in simplest form.

mc.explain: Rewrite {{1/2}} as {{2/4}}, then {{2/4}} + {{1/4}} = {{3/4}}. Adding tops AND bottoms to get {{2/6}} is wrong — the denominator only names the size of the pieces.
Rewrite {{2/3}} as {{4/6}}, then {{4/6}} − {{1/6}} = {{3/6}} = {{1/2}}. Subtracting the numerators and denominators separately gives {{1/3}}, which is incorrect.

mc.q: Which fraction is equivalent to {{3/4}}?
mc.explain: Multiply top and bottom by 3: {{3/4}} = {{9/12}}. Adding the same number to top and bottom (like {{4/5}}) changes the value — you must multiply, not add.
The common denominator is 24: {{9/24}} + {{8/24}} = {{17/24}}. {{4/11}} comes from adding straight across, and {{4/24}} forgets to convert the numerators.

mc.q: Without computing exactly, {{7/8}} + {{1/12}} is closest to which number?
mc.explain: {{7/8}} is close to 1 and {{1/12}} is close to 0, so the sum is close to 1. Benchmarks let you estimate without finding a common denominator.
Wholes: 2 + 1 = 3. Fractions: {{3/12}} + {{8/12}} = {{11/12}}. So the sum is 3{{11/12}}. Adding straight across gives the wrong {{3/7}}.

mc.q: Maya ran {{5/6}} of a mile. Jon ran {{2/3}} of a mile. How much farther did Maya run?
mc.explain: Rewrite {{2/3}} as {{4/6}}: {{5/6}} − {{4/6}} = {{1/6}} mile. Subtracting numerators without converting first gives the wrong answer {{1/2}}.
As improper fractions: {{25/6}} − {{15/6}} = {{10/6}} = 1{{2/3}}. Flipping the subtraction to {{1/2}} − {{1/6}} gives 2{{1/3}}, a common regrouping mistake.

mc.q: A snack mix uses {{1/2}} cup of raisins, {{1/3}} cup of peanuts, and {{1/4}} cup of pretzels. How many cups of mix is that in all?
mc.explain: The common denominator is 12: {{6/12}} + {{4/12}} + {{3/12}} = {{13/12}} = 1{{1/12}} cups. Adding straight across ({{3/9}} = {{1/3}}) is far too small.

mc.q: What fraction added to {{3/4}} gives a sum of 1{{5/12}}?

open.q: Add. Write your answer as a mixed number in simplest form: {{5/6}} + {{3/4}}

open.solution: The least common denominator of 10 and 4 is 20. Rewrite: {{7/10}} = {{14/20}} and {{1/4}} = {{5/20}}. Subtract: {{14/20}} − {{5/20}} = {{9/20}}, which is already in simplest form.

open.q: Leah drank {{3/8}} of a carton of milk and her brother drank {{1/6}} of the same carton. What fraction of the carton did they drink together?
open.solution: The least common denominator of 8 and 6 is 24. Rewrite: {{3/8}} = {{9/24}} and {{1/6}} = {{4/24}}. Add: {{9/24}} + {{4/24}} = {{13/24}} of the carton.

open.q: Add. Write your answer as a mixed number in simplest form: 3{{2/5}} + 2{{3/4}}
open.solution: Add the wholes: 3 + 2 = 5. Add the fractions with denominator 20: {{8/20}} + {{15/20}} = {{23/20}} = 1{{3/20}}. Combine: 5 + 1{{3/20}} = 6{{3/20}}.

open.q: Tanya has 5{{1/3}} yards of ribbon. She uses 2{{3/4}} yards for a school banner. How much ribbon is left?

challenge.q: A hiking club walks a trail over three days. On day 1 they hike {{2/5}} of the trail, and on day 2 they hike {{1/4}} of the trail. The 4{{1/5}} miles left is day 3's hike. How long is the whole trail?
challenge.solution: Fraction hiked in the first two days: {{2/5}} + {{1/4}} = {{8/20}} + {{5/20}} = {{13/20}}. So {{7/20}} of the trail remains, and that equals 4{{1/5}} = {{21/5}} miles. Since 7 twentieths equal {{21/5}} miles, one twentieth is {{21/5}} ÷ 7 = {{3/5}} mile. The whole trail is 20 × {{3/5}} = 12 miles. Check: {{13/20}} of 12 = 7.8 miles, and 7.8 + 4.2 = 12. ✔

concepts.title: Fractions as Division
know: A fraction IS a division problem: {{a/b}} means a ÷ b. For example, {{3/4}} = 3 ÷ 4.
When you share things equally, divide: 3 pizzas shared by 4 people means each person gets 3 ÷ 4 = {{3/4}} of a pizza.
If the top number is bigger than the bottom, the answer is more than 1 — write it as a mixed number, like {{9/2}} = 4{{1/2}}.
The number being shared goes on top; the number of equal groups goes on the bottom. Don't flip them!
Check your answer with multiplication: if 3 ÷ 4 = {{3/4}}, then 4 × {{3/4}} should equal 3.

mc.q: Which division problem does the fraction {{5/8}} represent?
mc.explain: A fraction means the top number divided by the bottom number, so {{5/8}} = 5 ÷ 8. Writing 8 ÷ 5 flips the numbers and gives a value greater than 1.

mc.q: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 4 friends. How much pizza does each friend get?
mc.explain: Each friend gets 3 ÷ 4 = {{3/4}} of a pizza. {{4/3}} flips the division — each person can't get more than one whole pizza when there are fewer pizzas than people.

mc.q: Which fraction equals 7 ÷ 10?
mc.explain: The first number in the division goes on top: 7 ÷ 10 = {{7/10}}. {{10/7}} is the inverted fraction and 70 comes from multiplying instead of dividing.

mc.q: Write 9 ÷ 2 as a mixed number.
mc.explain: 9 ÷ 2 = {{9/2}}. Since 2 × 4 = 8 with 1 left over, {{9/2}} = 4{{1/2}}. Answering 4 drops the leftover half instead of sharing it.

mc.q: Four friends share 5 sandwiches equally. How much does each friend get?
mc.explain: Each friend gets 5 ÷ 4 = {{5/4}} = 1{{1/4}} sandwiches. {{4/5}} flips the division — with more sandwiches than friends, each person gets more than 1.

mc.q: A 2-yard rope is cut into 3 equal pieces for a craft project. How long is each piece?
mc.explain: Each piece is 2 ÷ 3 = {{2/3}} yard. {{1/3}} ignores that there are 2 whole yards to share, and 1{{1/2}} comes from flipping the division to 3 ÷ 2.

mc.q: The fraction {{23/5}} is between which two whole numbers?
mc.explain: {{23/5}} = 23 ÷ 5 = 4{{3/5}}, which is between 4 and 5. Since 5 × 4 = 20 and 5 × 5 = 25, the answer must fall between 4 and 5.

mc.q: A baker splits 14 pounds of dough equally into 4 loaves. How much dough is in each loaf?
mc.explain: 14 ÷ 4 = {{14/4}} = 3{{2/4}} = 3{{1/2}} pounds. Answering 3 pounds drops the 2 leftover pounds, which must still be split among the 4 loaves.

mc.q: Which situation is represented by 4 ÷ 6?
choices: 4 granola bars shared equally by 6 hikers
6 granola bars shared equally by 4 hikers
4 boxes with 6 granola bars in each
mc.explain: 4 ÷ 6 means 4 things split into 6 equal shares — each hiker gets {{4/6}} = {{2/3}} of a bar. The other choices show 6 ÷ 4 or multiplication.

mc.q: A 5-pound bag of trail mix is divided equally among 8 campers. How many pounds do 3 of the campers get altogether?
mc.explain: Each camper gets 5 ÷ 8 = {{5/8}} pound. Three campers get 3 × {{5/8}} = {{15/8}} = 1{{7/8}} pounds. {{5/8}} pound is only one camper's share.

open.q: Write 11 ÷ 4 as a mixed number in simplest form.
Three friends share 8 fruit strips equally. How many fruit strips does each friend get? Write your answer as a mixed number.
open.solution: Each friend gets 8 ÷ 3 = {{8/3}} fruit strips. Since 3 × 2 = 6 with 2 left over, {{8/3}} = 2{{2/3}}. Each friend gets 2 whole strips plus {{2/3}} of the last two strips split three ways.

open.q: An art teacher shares 5 pounds of clay equally among 12 students. What fraction of a pound does each student get?
open.solution: Sharing 5 pounds among 12 students means 5 ÷ 12 = {{5/12}} pound each. The amount being shared goes on top, the number of shares on the bottom. Check: 12 × {{5/12}} = 5. ✔

open.q: A 9-foot sandwich is cut into 6 equal pieces for a team picnic. How long is each piece?
Marcus pours 7 gallons of juice equally into 2 coolers for field day. How many gallons go into each cooler?
open.solution: Each cooler gets 7 ÷ 2 = {{7/2}} gallons. Since 2 × 3 = 6 with 1 left over, {{7/2}} = 3{{1/2}} gallons. The leftover gallon is split in half between the two coolers.

challenge.q: On Monday, 4 pizzas were shared equally by 6 kids. On Tuesday, 3 pizzas were shared equally by 4 kids. On which day did each kid get more pizza — and how much more?
challenge.solution: Monday: each kid got 4 ÷ 6 = {{4/6}} = {{2/3}} of a pizza. Tuesday: each kid got 3 ÷ 4 = {{3/4}} of a pizza. Compare with a common denominator of 12: {{2/3}} = {{8/12}} and {{3/4}} = {{9/12}}. Tuesday's share is bigger, and the difference is {{9/12}} − {{8/12}} = {{1/12}} of a pizza.

concepts.title: Multiplying Fractions & Scaling
know: To multiply a fraction by a whole number, multiply the whole number by the numerator: {{2/3}} × 6 = {{12/3}} = 4.
To multiply two fractions, multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: {{2/3}} × {{1/4}} = {{2/12}} = {{1/6}}.
"Of" means multiply: {{3/4}} of 24 is {{3/4}} × 24.
Area still works with fractions: a rectangle {{1/2}} m by {{2/3}} m has area {{1/2}} × {{2/3}} = {{1/3}} square meter.
Scaling: multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes a number smaller; multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes it bigger — no computing needed!
To multiply mixed numbers, first rewrite them as improper fractions: 2{{1/2}} = {{5/2}}.

mc.explain: {{1/3}} × 12 = {{12/3}} = 4, the same as 12 ÷ 3. Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes the answer smaller than 12, so 36 can't be right.
Multiply across: {{2/3}} × {{1/4}} = {{2/12}} = {{1/6}}. {{3/7}} comes from adding tops and bottoms, and 2{{2/3}} comes from flipping and dividing instead.

mc.q: Without multiplying, which statement is true about {{4/5}} × 60?
mc.explain: {{4/5}} is less than 1, so multiplying 60 by it shrinks it — the product must be less than 60. Only multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes it bigger.
Multiply across: {{3/4}} × {{2/5}} = {{6/20}} = {{3/10}}. {{5/9}} adds instead of multiplying, and 1{{7/8}} comes from flipping {{2/5}} and dividing.

mc.q: A sticker is a rectangle {{1/2}} meter long and {{2/3}} meter wide. What is its area?
mc.explain: Area = length × width = {{1/2}} × {{2/3}} = {{2/6}} = {{1/3}} square meter. 1{{1/6}} comes from adding the sides, and 2{{1/3}} is the perimeter, not the area.
5 × {{2/3}} = {{10/3}} = 3{{1/3}}. Multiplying the denominator too (5 × 2 over 5 × 3) just gives back {{2/3}}, which is a common mistake.

mc.q: There are 24 students in Ms. Rivera's class, and {{3/4}} of them bought tickets to the school carnival. How many students bought tickets?
mc.explain: "Of" means multiply: {{3/4}} × 24 = {{72/4}} = 18. Answering 6 finds {{1/4}} of the class instead, and 32 divides by 3 then multiplies by 4.

mc.q: Without multiplying, which product is GREATER than {{5/6}}?
mc.explain: {{3/2}} is greater than 1, so {{5/6}} × {{3/2}} is greater than {{5/6}}. Multiplying by {{1/2}} or {{2/3}} shrinks it, and multiplying by 1 leaves it unchanged.

mc.q: One batch of muffins needs 1{{1/3}} cups of flour. Deja is making 2{{1/2}} batches for a bake sale. How much flour does she need?
mc.explain: Convert first: {{4/3}} × {{5/2}} = {{20/6}} = 3{{1/3}} cups. Multiplying wholes and fractions separately (2 × 1 and {{1/2}} × {{1/3}}) gives 2{{1/6}}, which misses two partial products.

mc.q: A garden plot is 3{{1/2}} feet long and 2{{1/4}} feet wide. What is its area?
mc.explain: Convert to improper fractions: {{7/2}} × {{9/4}} = {{63/8}} = 7{{7/8}} square feet. Multiplying only 3 × 2 and {{1/2}} × {{1/4}} gives 6{{1/8}}, and 11{{1/2}} is the perimeter.

open.q: Multiply. Write your answer in simplest form: {{4/5}} × {{3/8}}
open.solution: Multiply the numerators and the denominators: {{4/5}} × {{3/8}} = {{12/40}}. Simplify by dividing top and bottom by 4: {{12/40}} = {{3/10}}.

open.q: Theo has 18 marbles, and {{2/3}} of them are blue. How many marbles are blue?
open.solution: "{{2/3}} of 18" means {{2/3}} × 18 = {{36/3}} = 12. You can also think: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 marbles in each third, and 2 × 6 = 12 blue marbles.

open.q: A doormat is a rectangle {{5/6}} yard long and {{3/4}} yard wide. What is its area in square yards?
open.solution: Area = length × width = {{5/6}} × {{3/4}} = {{15/24}}. Simplify by dividing top and bottom by 3: {{15/24}} = {{5/8}} square yard.

open.q: Each bag of apples weighs 1{{3/4}} pounds. How much do 8 bags weigh in all?
open.solution: Convert to an improper fraction: 1{{3/4}} = {{7/4}}. Multiply: {{7/4}} × 8 = {{56/4}} = 14 pounds. Check: 8 × 1 = 8 and 8 × {{3/4}} = 6, and 8 + 6 = 14. ✔

open.q: Without multiplying, tell whether {{7/8}} × 456 is greater than, less than, or equal to 456. Explain how you know.
open.solution: {{7/8}} is less than 1, and multiplying a number by a fraction less than 1 always gives a product smaller than that number. So {{7/8}} × 456 is less than 456 — no computation needed.

challenge.q: A movie poster is 2{{1/2}} feet wide. Its height is 1{{1/5}} times its width. What is the area of the poster in square feet?
challenge.solution: Step 1 — find the height: 2{{1/2}} × 1{{1/5}} = {{5/2}} × {{6/5}} = {{30/10}} = 3 feet. Step 2 — find the area: width × height = {{5/2}} × 3 = {{15/2}} = 7{{1/2}} square feet. Scaling check: the height factor 1{{1/5}} is a little more than 1, so the height (3 ft) should be a little more than the width (2{{1/2}} ft). ✔

concepts.title: Dividing with Unit Fractions
know: A unit fraction has 1 on top, like {{1/2}}, {{1/3}}, or {{1/4}}.
Unit fraction ÷ whole number: sharing a piece makes SMALLER pieces. {{1/2}} ÷ 3 = {{1/6}}, because splitting a half into 3 equal parts makes sixths.
Whole number ÷ unit fraction asks "how many small pieces fit?" 4 ÷ {{1/3}} = 12, because each whole holds 3 thirds.
These two kinds of problems are different — read carefully to see which number is being split up.
Check with multiplication: if {{1/2}} ÷ 3 = {{1/6}}, then {{1/6}} × 3 must equal {{1/2}}.

mc.explain: Splitting a half into 3 equal parts makes pieces of size {{1/6}}. Check: {{1/6}} × 3 = {{3/6}} = {{1/2}}. Answering 6 divides in the wrong direction.
Each whole contains 3 thirds, so 4 wholes contain 4 × 3 = 12 thirds. {{1/12}} confuses this with {{1/3}} ÷ 4, and 1{{1/3}} divides 4 by 3 instead.

mc.q: How many {{1/4}}-cup servings of yogurt are in 3 cups?
mc.explain: 3 ÷ {{1/4}} = 3 × 4 = 12 servings, because each cup holds 4 quarter-cups. {{3/4}} multiplies 3 × {{1/4}} instead of asking how many quarters fit.
Splitting one fifth into 4 equal parts makes pieces of size {{1/20}}. Answering 20 flips it to 4 ÷ {{1/5}}, and {{4/5}} multiplies instead of dividing.
6 ÷ {{1/2}} asks how many halves are in 6 wholes: 6 × 2 = 12. Answering 3 divides 6 by 2, which is dividing by 2 instead of by {{1/2}}.

mc.q: There is {{1/3}} of a pan of cornbread left. Two friends split it equally. What fraction of the whole pan does each friend get?
mc.explain: {{1/3}} ÷ 2 = {{1/6}} of the whole pan, since splitting a third in half makes sixths. Check: {{1/6}} × 2 = {{1/3}}. {{2/3}} multiplies by 2 instead of dividing.

mc.q: Which multiplication equation can be used to CHECK that {{1/4}} ÷ 5 = {{1/20}}?
mc.explain: Division and multiplication undo each other: quotient × divisor = dividend, so {{1/20}} × 5 must give back {{1/4}}. It does: {{5/20}} = {{1/4}}. ✔

mc.q: Priya has 5 yards of ribbon. Each bow uses {{1/6}} yard. How many bows can she make?
mc.explain: 5 ÷ {{1/6}} = 5 × 6 = 30 bows, because each yard makes 6 bows. {{5/6}} comes from multiplying 5 × {{1/6}} instead of asking how many sixths fit in 5.

mc.q: A pitcher holds {{1/2}} gallon of lemonade, poured equally into 8 glasses. What fraction of a gallon is in each glass?
mc.explain: {{1/2}} ÷ 8 = {{1/16}} gallon per glass, since splitting a half into 8 parts makes sixteenths. Check: {{1/16}} × 8 = {{8/16}} = {{1/2}}. ✔ Answering 16 flips the division.

mc.q: Nora has 2 cups of sprinkles. Each cupcake gets {{1/8}} cup. She decorates as many of her 20 cupcakes as she can. How many cupcakes get NO sprinkles?
mc.explain: Step 1: 2 ÷ {{1/8}} = 2 × 8 = 16 cupcakes get sprinkles. Step 2: 20 − 16 = 4 cupcakes get none. Answering 16 stops after the first step.

open.solution: Splitting one sixth into 3 equal parts makes pieces that are 3 times smaller: {{1/6}} ÷ 3 = {{1/18}}. Check with multiplication: {{1/18}} × 3 = {{3/18}} = {{1/6}}. ✔

open.q: Sam has 8 cups of trail mix and puts it into {{1/4}}-cup snack bags. How many snack bags can he fill?
open.solution: This asks how many quarter-cups are in 8 cups: 8 ÷ {{1/4}} = 8 × 4 = 32 bags, because each cup fills 4 bags. Check: 32 × {{1/4}} = 8 cups. ✔

open.q: Half of a garden bed will be split equally among 4 vegetables. What fraction of the whole garden bed does each vegetable get?
open.solution: Each vegetable gets {{1/2}} ÷ 4 of the bed. Splitting a half into 4 equal parts makes eighths, so each vegetable gets {{1/8}}. Check: {{1/8}} × 4 = {{4/8}} = {{1/2}}. ✔
7 ÷ {{1/3}} asks how many thirds are in 7 wholes. Each whole contains 3 thirds, so 7 × 3 = 21. Check: 21 × {{1/3}} = 7. ✔

open.q: A carpenter cuts a 9-foot board into {{1/2}}-foot blocks for a game. How many blocks does she get?
open.solution: This asks how many half-feet are in 9 feet: 9 ÷ {{1/2}} = 9 × 2 = 18 blocks, because each foot makes 2 blocks. Check: 18 × {{1/2}} = 9 feet. ✔

challenge.q: Priya has 3 cups of lemonade mix. Each pitcher of lemonade needs {{1/4}} cup of mix, and each pitcher fills 6 glasses. Priya needs 60 glasses of lemonade for field day. Does she have enough mix? How many glasses over or short is she?
challenge.answer: Yes — 12 glasses more than she needs
challenge.solution: Step 1: pitchers she can make = 3 ÷ {{1/4}} = 3 × 4 = 12 pitchers. Step 2: glasses she can fill = 12 × 6 = 72 glasses. Step 3: compare to what she needs: 72 − 60 = 12. She has enough, with 12 extra glasses' worth of lemonade. (She actually only needs 10 pitchers, which use 10 × {{1/4}} = 2{{1/2}} cups of mix.)
